ALL MY BEST FRIENDS BY GEORGE BURNS with David Fisher Putnam, 320 pages, $23.50 REVIEW BY ROBERT CUSHMAN A book of anecdotes, like a dictionary of quotations, is not something to be read. It is to be consulted, dipped into, rifled. A browsers delight, it is guaranteed to put a reviewer in a foul temper. He has to plow through it, thinking about all the real books in which anecdotes have been welcome diversions from the serious business of narrative and analysis. He knew he'd have to pay for them some day. Here is that day, and if he doesn't watch his language he'll find himself dragging out the old image of an indigestible meal entirely composed of hors doeuvres.
